gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the power each pick needs from a USB-C power bank: the Nebula Capsule 3 needs PD 20 V/2.25 A (45 W), the XGIMI MoGo 4 needs 65–150 W at 20 V (20 V/3.25 A minimum), the Aurzen ZIP needs a 24 W+ PD adapter, and the Nebula Mars 3 Air has no USB-C input at all. It only charges through a 19 V/4.74 A barrel plug, and its manual says to use only the maker's adapter.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides' MoGo 4 vs Capsule 3 page (rank 8). It says the MoGo 4 'supports USB-C charging using PD 3.0' and warns that 'not every USB-C bank will supply the required voltage and wattage', but it gives no watt or volt figure for either model, and for the Capsule 3 it quotes a listing for the Laser variant. I could not read the cited Wirecutter page: the proxy URL shows only a 'stop using this as a proxy' notice. The RTINGS page also showed no review text. So it's unverified whether Wirecutter, which ChatGPT credits for the Mars 3 Air pick, mentions that the Mars 3 Air can't be charged over USB-C. ChatGPT's answer recommends the Mars 3 Air as 'battery-powered' and lists 'Travel / camping' as a use case without giving any power-bank limits.
decides: For a shopper who wants to top up or run the projector from a power bank (travel, camping, car), this rules out the Mars 3 Air, which needs its 90 W DC adapter or an AC outlet. It also splits the rest. A 45 W PD bank is enough for the Capsule 3 but below the MoGo 4's stated 65 W floor. The MoGo 4 / MoGo 4 Laser need a 20 V bank of 65 W or more. The Aurzen ZIP runs on 24 W+ PD and can project while charging, but it has no HDMI port or built-in Netflix. That confirms the Capsule 3 as the 'smallest practical' pick for people who already own a mid-size bank, and the MoGo 4 as the pick for people with a 65 W+ laptop bank.
